chunks: God has indeed heard the words of those who said: 'God is a pauper whereas we are rich.' We shall make a note of their words, and the murders of the prophets they committed unjustly, and say to them: 'Now taste the agony of burning.'

key_terms.إِنَ اللَّهَ: God is (in the context of being in need)

ai.seo_question: What did the disbelievers say about God being poor, and what is the consequence?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the Banu Qurayza or the broader Jewish tribes of Medina who accused God of poverty due to His command for Zakat, while also highlighting their unjust slaying of prophets like Yahya and Isa. It serves as a divine record of their verbal arrogance and physical persecution of the righteous, culminating in the promise of the 'burning fire' (Nar al-Sa'ir) as retribution for their dual transgression of word and deed.
